params.body:
## Why

`phpunit` is red on main since midnight, and on every branch opened from it. Not a regression in behaviour: `BiddingMailsTest::the daily mail holds the biddings of the past day` sets the clock to 18 September with `Carbon::setTestNow` and puts its vehicles on the 17th, but the query behind the daily mail reads `date('Y-m-d', strtotime('- 1 day'))`, the machine's clock, which Carbon cannot move. The test passed on the day it was written (PR #556) and fails every day after.

## What changed

`ExportVehicleRepository`: `now()->subDay()->toDateString()` and `now()->toDateString()` instead of `date()`. In production the two clocks are the same, so the mail keeps sending exactly what it sent; what changes is that a test can hold the day still.

Finding `2026-09-19-dagmail-query-las-de-machineklok` records the class of defect: a query a test must be able to pin does not read the machine's clock.

## Tests

`BiddingMailsTest|BiddingFunnelTest|BiddingTest|ScheduleTest`: 31 tests, 223 assertions, green (the daily-mail test was the failing one). Guards `Rules*|FindingsIssues`: 20 tests. `php bin/rules-sources`: Geen problemen.
params.title: The daily export reads the application clock (main is red without it)
